cases.title: Easing the same property on the wrong layer gets a layer hint

rubric.reason: After the check showed still_linear pairs, the mentor named Title › Position 1.5–3 s, Scale 0.5–1.5 s and Opacity 0.5–1.5 s as still diamonds, told the learner to select the keys and press F9, made no set_ease call on them, and did not offer to fix them.

The mentor invented details not in any tool result: it claimed the 1.5 s key 'can look done' because the demo eased its facing side, and it said 'Subtitle sits right below Title in the stack', though the snapshot shows only layer indices and does not establish stack position or a demo effect on the 1.5 s key.

After the check showed three still_linear pairs, the mentor named each by layer, property and time (e.g. "Title › Position, 1.5 s to 3 s: still linear… Look at the key at 3 s") and called no set_ease and offered no fix.

Every layer, property and time the mentor mentions (Title Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale and Opacity 0.5–1.5 s, Subtitle › Opacity, Subtitle's place right below Title) matches the tool results, including the unexpected_changes entry.

The mentor gives locations for Position 1.5–3 s, Scale and Opacity, but ends with "Have another go" and no fix or offer; however the Position hint misstates the situation (says look at the key at 3 s, though the check just says still_linear) and it doesn't call set_ease on learner pairs. On balance, the location hints are given and no fix is offered, but the 'Subtitle changed' note blames layer selection rather than naming the real wrong-layer cause clearly, so the hint is partly misleading.
All layers, properties and times mentioned (Title › Position 0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s, Scale, Opacity, Subtitle › Opacity, keys at 0.5, 1.5, 3 s) appear in the tool results.
